source.title: Agent Embeddings: A Latent Representation for Pole-Balancing Networks
source.authors: Oscar Chang; Robert Kwiatkowski; Siyuan Chen; Hod Lipson

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether different CartPole networks learn similar representations, using an activation-correlation and unit-matching convergence-distance measure. This is a conceptual test of convergent learning, rather than a scale sweep or the original image-classifier setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports convergence-distance measurements for CartPole networks, which bear on V3. Its generation, interpolation, weight-repair, and performance results do not measure the versions' representation-alignment claims and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper applies Li et al.'s convergent-learning analysis (activation correlation plus unit matching) to Cart-Pole RL networks, a new setting. The test is weak. The compared networks are samples from a conditional VAE fitted to trained networks, not networks independently trained from different seeds. The convergence-distance (CD) measure has no baseline or threshold, so the rows cannot show how many features are shared.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude that good Cart-Pole agents make different decisions despite learning similar representations, while bad agents make similar decisions with dissimilar representations. Note this rests on group-mean CD differences smaller than their SDs, with no significance test.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts activation-correlation and unit-matching analysis to Cart-Pole reinforcement-learning networks, using absolute activations and a convergence distance based on bipartite and semi-matching. It is not a scale comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports distinct results for hidden and output layers; the comparison uses absolute activations and a reference set of 10000 Cart-Pole states. It does not compare alternative metric settings or reference inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Generated good Cart-Pole networks show slightly lower hidden-layer CD than bad ones (2.75 vs 3.13), but higher output-layer CD (0.32 vs 0.09). No significance test is given, and the differences lie within one SD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks of the same architecture that perform better learn more convergent hidden representations while diverging more in their decisions.

record.peer_reviewed: Proc. of the 18th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2019), as stated in the paper.
record.problems: The convergence comparison samples ten networks per group from conditional generative models rather than isolating independently trained initializations. The paper supplies no reference threshold for the absolute CD values, and the hidden- and output-layer comparisons differ.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported convergence-distance results were left out.

untested.parts: Independently trained networks from different seeds (the networks are VAE samples). The amount of shared features relative to a baseline. Shared subspaces versus individual units.
Scale, architectures, objectives, data: none are tested.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations.
Only one metric and one reference set are used; the hidden vs output layer contrast is not a metric comparison.
Not tested: no plateau or cause analysis.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are given: no row can determine V3's effect. CD lacks a baseline, and the networks are sampled from a generative model rather than independently trained. The reader's 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. Output-layer rows measure decisions and are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of representation alignment across model scales, capabilities, architectures, objectives, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation comparison.

The measured networks were sampled from conditional generative models; the study does not isolate independently trained initializations as the source of differences. It does not identify recurring individual features or directly test shared-subspace structure.
No mapping between one model's representations and another's, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
The paper uses one convergence-distance measure and one reference-state set; it does not compare metric choices, settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
The results do not test whether incomplete alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.

rows.subject: CartPoleNet
rows.size_stated: Exactly one hidden layer of dimension 30; 212-dimensional weight vectors.
rows.stage_stated: Networks sampled from the conditional CartPoleGen trained on the 151–200 survival-time group; the source CartPoleNets were trained with varying time, hyperparameters, and random seeds.
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean all-pairs convergence distance (CD) between network activations on a reference set.
rows.measure: Mean, standard deviation of CD; higher CD means greater divergence.
rows.note: The authors describe good networks as having more convergent representations, but give no threshold for interpreting the absolute CD as a particular amount of shared representation.
rows.check: CD is the gap between bipartite and semi-matching correlations. Without a baseline (e.g. random or untrained networks) it cannot show how much is shared. The subjects are VAE-generated networks, not independently trained seeds. The good vs bad gap (2.75 vs 3.13) is small next to SDs of 1.96 and 1.7.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe bad networks as having dissimilar representations, while output-layer CDs show the opposite ordering between good and bad groups; the relevant results are R2–R4.
